correctness.rationale: The Euclidean normal cone of each K_{p,q} zonotope vertex is a graphic-arrangement chamber union: sorting isotropic Gaussian coordinates is uniform over (p+q)! orders, and consecutive same-partite vertices form blocks freely permutable inside runs. This gives angle prod_i(a_i!)prod_j(b_j!)/(p+q)!, orientation multiplicity p!q!/prod factorials, and collision sum C=sum(angle^2). The formal alternating-run series is F(x)F(y)(2+F(x)+F(y))/(1-F(x)F(y)), with F(t)=sum j! t^j; no analytic convergence is presumed. Fixed q means at most q+1 first-class blocks. For k>=2, merging a pair proves S_k(p)<=S_2(p)=O(1/p); one first-class block contributes p!q! H_q. This proves p^{2q}C->(q!)^2 H_q, NOT uniform in q. The min-angle smoothing and two-block max formulas match the block inequalities. An independent enumeration of ALL labeled orders for (1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(3,2),(3,3) gives 1/2,5/18,7/72,47/1200,9/800, agreeing with the combinatorial series, but is finite corroboration, not proof for all p,q.

Only the fixed-q asymptotic is proved; not simultaneous growth.

value.rationale: A natural geometric sampling statistic on graph zonotopes: probability that two independent Euclidean supporting objectives have identical maximizing vertices. Exact angular spectrum/weighted second moment provides concentration information not contained in acyclic-orientation counts. The counterintuitive polynomial effective-support size versus exponentially many vertices has a sharp fixed-partite constant (q!)^2 H_q. Both the specified model and invariant have intrinsic motivation, with potential use in randomized vertex enumeration.
residual_risks: The second collision law is restricted to Euclidean metric and complete-bipartite graphs; its numerical coefficient is not asserted for arbitrary zonotopes.

limitations: Intrinsic Euclidean K_{p,q}, p,q>=1, fixed q then p->infinity; complete angle spectrum and extremal-angle side results; no proof of mixed-growth asymptotics or global priority.
Prior coverage and inaccessibility qualifications are explicit in O; bounded literature search is not a proof of absolute priority.
